thread:
maria-cs: Heads-up — Veridian Health renewal is in 6 weeks. I ran the health check and there are two latency blips in the last 90 days that might push them into a credit band. Need engineering + SRE to confirm numbers and help assemble evidence for the renewal comms. @oliver-ps @jana-sre @kai-oncall :eyes:

oliver-ps: Thanks Maria. Can you confirm which metric we should use for the credit calc — p95 across their primary inference route (route: /v1/generate/veridian-main) or global p95 across all routes? Also do we exclude scheduled maint windows?

maria-cs: Use route-level p95 for /v1/generate/veridian-main for the credit threshold. Exclude scheduled maint windows and the two maintenance start/ends listed in the onboarding notes (2025-11-12 0200-0300 UTC, 2026-01-08 0100-0130 UTC). I sketched a quick credit calc: credit = max(0, (SLO_target - observed_uptime) * monthly_commit * 0.01). But we need verified uptime and p95 latency snapshots.

jana-sre: I can pull the metrics. Query you can run in Observability:
```
metrics.query(
  "p95_latency",
  route="/v1/generate/veridian-main",
  timeframe="90d",
  exclude_windows=["2025-11-12T02:00Z/2025-11-12T03:00Z","2026-01-08T01:00Z/2026-01-08T01:30Z"]
)
```
That returns time-series plus aggregate p95 and uptime. I'll export CSV and attach to thread when done.

kai-oncall: Note — there was a degraded node event on 2026-02-14 18:10 UTC that impacted tail latency for ~22m. It was caused by autoscaler thrash after a traffic spike. Should we exclude a short mitigation window where our fallback model served with higher latency? Ops prefers to mark it as a customer-impact incident in the evidence bundle (with RCA) rather than exclude it. Decision up to CS.

maria-cs: Mark it as an incident in the bundle but include the mitigations and timeline. Customer expects transparency. We should still calculate credits per the contract.

oliver-ps: I'll generate a p95 table and the tokenized request counts per hour. Two asks from my side: (1) confirm the exact SLA clause we apply (I think it's Section 3.2 — "Latency: p95 <= 800ms"), and (2) confirm month to use for monthly_commit in the credit formula (use average monthly spend over past 3 months?).

maria-cs: Correct, Section 3.2 p95 <= 800ms. Use the 3-month average commit. I'll pull finance numbers and DM them to you.

jana-sre: CSV export uploaded to the internal bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/veridian/2837654321/metrics_p95_uptime_90d.csv — includes per-route p50/ p95/ p99 and uptime pct. Also uploaded a traces sample: traces_veridian_q1.zip (first 500 samples).

deploy-bot: [system] Upload complete: s3://redwood-evidence/veridian/2837654321/metrics_p95_uptime_90d.csv :white_check_mark:

oliver-ps: Got the CSV. Preliminary numbers: observed uptime = 99.81% for the 90d window, observed route-level p95 = 860ms (above SLA). Using Maria's credit formula with 3-month avg commit = $12,000, that implies provisional credit = (99.9 - 99.81) * 12000 * 0.01 = $10.8 -> round to $11? That looks small; are we scaling by percent correctly?

maria-cs: Hmm our contract credits are in dollars rounded to nearest $50. Can someone run the official credit calculator script? I think the formula should be: credit = monthly_commit * min(1, max(0, (SLO_pct - observed_pct) / SLO_pct)) and then apply the credit tiers from the contract.

jana-sre: Running the official calc now with observed_uptime=99.81, SLO=99.9, monthly_commit=12000. I'll post the tiered result in ~10m. Also attaching the incident timeline and RCA excerpt in the evidence bundle.

maria-cs: Next steps: (1) Jana — finalize the CSV + incident doc, (2) Oliver — run the official calc and draft the customer-facing paragraph with the credit amount and explanation, (3) Kai — advise if we want to offer a one-time operational remediation (e.g., reserved capacity bump for 30 days) as a goodwill gesture. I'll draft the renewal note after we have numbers.

kai-oncall: I support offering a 30d reserved-capacity trial if the credit exceeds $500. If credit is tiny, just offer the standard SLO remediation plan.

oliver-ps: Draft for customer email (please tweak):
"Hi Veridian team — we've completed a review of your performance over the past 90 days. Your route /v1/generate/veridian-main observed p95 latency of 860ms against an SLA of 800ms; observed uptime for the window is 99.81% (SLA target 99.9%). Per Section 3.2 of your contract, this results in a one-time credit of $50. We're also offering a 30-day reserved-capacity trial to stabilize latency during peak windows. Please let us know if you'd like us to apply the credit to next invoice or as a service credit"

maria-cs: That draft looks good — please keep it factual and include the attached evidence bundle. I'll hold the renewal outreach until we finalize numbers. :white_check_mark:

jana-sre: Official calc result posted to thread: tiered_credit: $50 (applies under contract tier 2). Evidence bundle path: s3://redwood-evidence/veridian/2837654321/evidence_bundle_v1.zip.

maria-cs: Amazing — thanks everyone. I'll prepare the renewal comms with the bundle and loop Legal for the credit application. Closing action items: oliver to send email template to customer after Legal ok, jana to mark incident in postmortems, kai to provision trial if approved. Follow-up meeting scheduled: Mon 09:30 PST. :calendar:
